title: Two-sided affine-space components and additive image invariance

newly_cached_primary_context.title: The Filtration Induced by a Locally Nilpotent Derivation
newly_cached_primary_context.author: Bachar Alhajjar
newly_cached_primary_context.portions_inspected: Introduction; Section 1.1 Definitions 1.1-1.3 and Lemma 1.4; Section 2 Definition 2.1 and the degree-zero kernel observation.
newly_cached_primary_context.role: Primary context for locally nilpotent derivation degrees and Makar-Limanov terminology. The exact degree facts needed here are fully reproved by the Leibniz formula. No action classification, finite-generation theorem, induced-derivation theorem or semi-rigid-ring result is imported.

direct_proof_arguments: the highest nonzero iterated Leibniz derivative makes the locally nilpotent degree additive, without a scalar kernel assumption
a moved principal affine-space component forces every geometric generic unit to be scalar
opposite affine-space quotient units make a degree-zero multiplier scalar in the two-sided component relation
a relative additive action moving the image equation gives a conjugate generic pencil without any positive generic filtration
rank-two reflexive descent supplies the global coordinate and the smooth minimal-label argument gives the carried inverse
joint constants equal to F imply scalar geometric units and an action moving the nonconstant image equation
nonautomorphy forces the image equation into the kernels of every relative additive action
natural polynomial-direction actions have exact joint kernel F[X], because removed rows dominate the multiplier components and forbid denominators
primitive multiplier content keeps X algebraically independent on every height-one generic fibre and descends F[X] intersection R to C[T,V,X]
the induced global source actions fix the original two source coordinates by finite separability over the Keller target field
